title: Composite of two adjunctions; the identity adjunction
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be categories, $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ left adjoint to $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ (unit $\eta_1:\mathrm{id}\to GF$, counit $\varepsilon_1:FG\to\mathrm{id}$) and $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ left adjoint to $I:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ (unit $\eta_2$, counit $\varepsilon_2$). The *composite adjunction* is the adjunction $H\circ F\dashv G\circ I$ with unit $\eta_A=G(\eta_{2,FA})\circ\eta_{1,A}:A\to GFA\to GIHFA$ and counit $\varepsilon_C=\varepsilon_{2,C}\circ H(\varepsilon_{1,IC}):HFGIC\to HIC\to C$; its hom bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(HFA,C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FA,IC)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,GIC)$ is the composite of the two hom bijections. The *identity adjunction* on $\mathcal A$ is $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\dashv\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ with identity unit and counit.
